title: Citemark accuracy report
header.demo: Unofficial demo built on Zulip's open-source help center (Apache-2.0). Not affiliated with Zulip.

measure.correct_answers.name: Correct answers
measure.correct_answers.definition: Answers with the right facts that contradicted nothing in the help center.
measure.right_source.name: Right source shown
measure.right_source.definition: Answers whose source points to the article the answer came from.
measure.correct_declines.name: Correctly said "not covered"
measure.correct_declines.definition: Questions the help center doesn't cover, where the bot said so instead of guessing.
measure.wrongly_declined.name: Wrongly said "not covered"
measure.wrongly_declined.definition: Questions the help center does cover, where the bot wrongly said it couldn't help. Lower is better.
measure.right_place.name: Looked in the right place
measure.right_place.definition: Questions where the right help-center section was among the 5 the bot read.
measure.honest_tickets.name: Honest tickets
measure.honest_tickets.definition: Ticket confirmations that matched a ticket really created in the helpdesk. Must be all of them.
measure.time_to_first_word.name: Time to first word
measure.time_to_first_word.definition: 95 of every 100 answers started within {seconds} s.
measure.cost.name: Cost per conversation
measure.cost.definition: ${cost} in AI costs, or ${per_thousand} per 1,000 conversations.
trace.heading: How to read this report: one question, traced
trace.intro: Every question in this report was checked in the same five steps. Here is one, from start to finish.
trace.step1: **1 · The question** — exactly as it was asked.
trace.step2: **2 · Where it looked** — the help-center sections the bot read before answering.
trace.step3: **3 · What it quoted** — the words it based its answer on, copied from the article.
trace.step4: **4 · What it answered** — the reply a customer would have seen.
trace.step5: **5 · The result** — checked against the answer a person wrote in advance.
trace.gap_step2: The right section wasn't among the ones it read.
trace.decline_step3: No quote, correctly. The help center doesn't cover this.
fix.heading.not_pass: What it would take to pass
fix.heading.baseline: What it would take to improve
fix.none: Nothing to fix: every question passed.
fix.owner.builder: Fixed by {builder_name} · about {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}
fix.owner.client: Fixed by {client} · {count, plural, one {# article} other {# articles}} to write
fix.owner.either: Fixed by {builder_name} or {client} · about {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}
fix.group.answered_should_decline.title: Answered instead of saying "not covered"
fix.group.answered_should_decline.what: The help center doesn't cover these, but the bot answered anyway. This is the most serious kind of failure. The fix is in the bot's instructions.
fix.group.declined_answerable.title: Wrongly said "not covered"
fix.group.declined_answerable.what: The help center covers these, but the bot said it couldn't help. The fix is in how it searches, or in how the article is worded.
fix.group.retrieval_miss.title: Looked in the wrong place
fix.group.retrieval_miss.what: The section with the answer wasn't among the ones the bot read. The fix is in how the help center is searched.
fix.group.wrong_citation.title: Right answer, wrong source
fix.group.wrong_citation.what: The answer was right, but its source pointed somewhere else. The fix is in how sources are matched to answers.
fix.group.wrong_answer.title: Right place, wrong answer
fix.group.wrong_answer.what: The bot read the right section but got the answer wrong. The fix is in the bot's instructions or the AI model.
fix.group.doc_gap.title: The help center is missing this
fix.group.doc_gap.what: Customers ask these, but no article answers them. Only {client} can write the missing articles.

method.heading: How this test was done
method.questions: {total} questions: {answerable} the help center answers, {partial} it answers in part, {ambiguous} that could mean more than one thing, and {should_decline} it doesn't cover. Frozen on {frozen_date}, before any tuning. Version {version}, fingerprint {fingerprint}.
method.authorship.demo: The questions and expected answers were drafted with AI help before the bot was built, then reviewed by {builder_name}, who changed {edited} of {total}. A wording check for questions that copy their article's phrasing flagged {flagged, plural, =0 {none} one {#, which was rewritten before the freeze} other {#, which were rewritten before the freeze}}. The draft and the frozen questions are both published, so the changes can be compared.
method.authorship.client: The questions are real ones {client}'s customers asked, taken from its support tickets. {builder_name} wrote the expected answers from the help center, and {client} reviewed them.
method.grading: Sources and "not covered" replies were checked automatically. Answers were graded by a separate AI model, {judge_model}, against the answers written in advance. To check that grader, {builder_name} graded all {graded} answers by hand, and the two agreed on {agreed} of {graded}.
method.grading_recheck: {builder_name} also graded {rechecked} answers from {recheck_models}, and the two agreed on {re_agreed} of {rechecked}.
method.grading_queue: {builder_name} also graded the {queued, plural, one {# answer} other {# answers}} to questions the AI model graded differently across the three runs, and those grades count instead of its own.
method.quotes: Every quote shown under an answer was copied word for word from the help center by the AI provider's citation feature. The bot can't change a quote.
method.abuse: It was also given {abuse_total} questions designed to make it invent a policy or promise, or follow instructions planted in a question or an article. It resisted {abuse_passed} of {abuse_total} in every run.
method.abuse_not_measured: Questions designed to make it invent a policy or promise, or follow instructions planted in a question or an article: Not measured yet.
method.runs: The questions were run three times, because an AI model doesn't answer in exactly the same way twice. Each number is the middle result of the three, and the range shows the lowest and highest.
method.cost: Costs are what the AI provider charged for these runs, at its prices on {price_date}.
method.speed: Speed was measured over {answer_starts} answers from the live bot.
method.setup: {setup}: version {prompt_version} of the bot's instructions, Citemark commit {commit}, runs {run_ids}.
signed.agreed: Pass mark agreed by {threshold_agreed_by} and {builder_name} on {threshold_date}.
